message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Fresh sweep completed for the daily run on 2026-06-10 IST, using the monitored product list in Products.txt. Several credible, product-matched vulnerability updates were reported or updated in the last 24 hours. The highest-priority items are Google Chrome's exploited V8 zero-day, Microsoft's large June Patch Tuesday release, Adobe Acrobat critical fixes, OpenSSL fixes, and Veeam Backup & Replication CVE-2026-44963.

**Finding 1: Google Chrome actively exploited V8 vulnerability**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: CVE-2026-11645
- Severity: High, as stated by Google/Chrome reporting; CISA also added it to KEV on June 9, 2026
- Description: Google released Chrome 149.0.7827.102/.103 for Windows and macOS, and 149.0.7827.102 for Linux, with 74 security fixes. CVE-2026-11645 is an out-of-bounds memory access issue in V8, and Google/CISA reporting says exploitation exists in the wild.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Google Chrome.
- Sources: Google Chrome Releases: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/06/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_0153744567.html; Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-561: https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/google-chrome-security-advisory-av26-561

**Finding 2: Microsoft June 2026 Patch Tuesday updates across Windows, Office, .NET, Defender, Visual Studio/VS Code, Edge, and related components**

- Product: Windows Server / Windows 10 / Microsoft Office / Microsoft .NET / Microsoft Defender / Visual Studio / Visual Studio Code / Microsoft Edge and related Microsoft components
- Issue: Multiple CVEs in the June 2026 Patch Tuesday release, including CVE-2026-45657, CVE-2026-47291, CVE-2026-44815, and multiple Microsoft Office RCE CVEs
- Severity: Microsoft/ZDI reporting lists numerous Critical and Important issues; ZDI highlights several CVSS 9.8 remote code execution vulnerabilities
- Description: Microsoft released a very large June security update set affecting Windows and Windows components, Office, Edge/Chromium-based components, .NET, Visual Studio, Defender, Hyper-V, BitLocker, and more. ZDI highlights CVE-2026-45657 in the Windows Kernel, CVE-2026-47291 in HTTP.sys, and CVE-2026-44815 in DHCP Client Service as high-impact remote code execution issues.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 10, Microsoft Office, Microsoft Edge, Microsoft .NET, Windows Defender, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, IIS, PowerShell, and Azure DevOps/TFS.
- Sources: BleepingComputer: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-june-2026-patch-tuesday-fixes-3-zero-day-200-flaws/; Zero Day Initiative: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/blog/2026/6/9/the-june-2026-security-update-review

**Finding 3: Adobe Acrobat and Reader critical and important vulnerabilities**

- Product: Adobe Acrobat / Acrobat Reader
- Issue: APSB26-63, including CVE-2026-47911 through CVE-2026-47926 and related CVEs listed by Adobe
- Severity: Critical and Important, as stated by Adobe
- Description: Adobe published security updates for Acrobat and Reader on Windows and macOS. The advisory includes multiple arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities, application denial-of-service issues, and memory exposure issues. Adobe says it is not aware of exploitation in the wild for these issues.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Adobe Acrobat.
- Source: Adobe APSB26-63: https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/acrobat/apsb26-63.html

**Finding 4: OpenSSL vulnerabilities published and Ubuntu OpenSSL packages updated**

- Product: OpenSSL / Ubuntu
- Issue: OpenSSL advisory and Ubuntu USN-8414-1 / USN-8414-2, including CVE-2026-45447, CVE-2026-34182, CVE-2026-42764, and others
- Severity: OpenSSL advisory includes Moderate and other severities; Ubuntu lists multiple CVEs but does not present a single overall severity on the notices index
- Description: OpenSSL published a June 9 security advisory covering multiple vulnerabilities. Ubuntu also published OpenSSL security notices for maintained and legacy Ubuntu releases, including issues that could lead to denial of service, integrity bypass, certificate/trust validation bypass, information exposure, or possible code execution depending on the affected code path.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes both OpenSSL and Ubuntu.
- Sources: oss-sec/OpenSSL advisory mirror: https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/861; Ubuntu Security Notices: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Finding 5: Veeam Backup & Replication remote code execution vulnerability**

- Product: Veeam Backup & Replication
- Issue: CVE-2026-44963
- Severity: Critical, CVSS v4 9.4, as stated by Veeam
- Description: Veeam disclosed an RCE vulnerability affecting Veeam Backup & Replication 12.3.2.4465 and earlier version 12 builds when the backup server is domain-joined. Veeam says version 13.x is not affected due to architectural changes.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Veeam.
- Sources: Veeam community advisory summary: https://community.veeam.com/cyber-security-space-95/cve-2026-44963-vulnerability-in-veeam-backup-replication-v12-cvss-v4-score-9-4-13447; BleepingComputer: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-veeam-vulnerability-exposes-backup-servers-to-rce-attacks/

**Possible matches needing review**

- Ubiquiti/UniFi: SC Media reported on June 8 that three already-fixed UniFi OS Server vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-34908, CVE-2026-34909, CVE-2026-34910) can be chained for unauthenticated RCE. The monitored list includes Ubiquiti/UniFi, but the exact publication time could not be verified as inside this 24-hour window, so this is listed for review rather than as a confirmed in-window finding. Source: https://www.scworld.com/brief/ubiquiti-unifi-os-server-vulnerabilities-allow-unauthenticated-remote-code-execution

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Chrome, internet-facing or server-side Microsoft systems, Acrobat deployments, OpenSSL/Ubuntu package exposure, and domain-joined Veeam Backup & Replication 12 servers. The Ubiquiti/UniFi item should be checked against local deployment and timing before treating it as part of today's confirmed digest.
